_meta.name: Purla cosmetic ingredient hazard table

field_definitions.inci: INCI name as it appears on EU/US ingredient labels.
field_definitions.risk: Editorial risk grade for Purla. NOT a regulatory value — see caveats.
field_definitions.reason: One-line rationale shown to the user.
field_definitions.basis: Bodies or instruments the grade draws on.
field_definitions.eu: Regulatory status under EU 1223/2009 and related instruments.
field_definitions.dose_dependent: True when the real risk depends on concentration or product type, which an ingredient list does not disclose.
field_definitions.disputed: True when authoritative sources reach different conclusions.
field_definitions.dispute_note: What the disagreement actually is. Show this instead of a grade where it matters.
field_definitions.confidence: Confidence in the regulatory detail as stated here, not in the risk grade.
field_definitions.risk_type: What the risk grade is actually about. 'environmental' means no regulator claims a dermal hazard - do not surface these as personal health risks. 'both' means there is a separate health finding as well as an environmental one.
field_definitions.eu_annex: Annexes of EU 1223/2009 this ingredient appears in, per this draft. Empty list means not in any annex (unrestricted, or restricted by another instrument such as REACH). This is the field the CosIng diff joins on.
field_definitions.declare_as: The single name that must appear in the ingredient list for a grouped entry. Match label text against this, not against the member INCI names.
field_definitions.covers_inci: Other INCI names sharing this Annex III entry and declared under the same name.
field_definitions.declaration_threshold: Concentration above which the allergen must be individually named. Uniform at 0.001% leave-on / 0.01% rinse-off across the 2023/1545 set.
field_definitions.eu_annex_ref: Annex III reference number, for joining to CosIng by entry rather than by name.
field_definitions.max_concentration: A real use limit on top of the declaration duty, where one exists.
field_definitions.peroxide_value_limit: Oxidation cap; the oxidation products are the sensitisers.
field_definitions.member_of: This entry is one member of a grouped Annex III entry. The primary entry named here carries the authoritative restriction; do not score both.

caveats: VERIFY BEFORE SHIPPING. Every eu field must be checked against the current CosIng Annex II-VI exports. The annexes change several times a year via Omnibus regulations; Omnibus VIII took effect 1 May 2026, Omnibus II on 18 May 2026, and Omnibus IX is in draft for 1 Feb 2027.

The EU 2023/1545 allergen expansion takes effect for new products on 31 July 2026: individually declarable fragrance allergens go from 26 to roughly 80. Labels scanned from now on will name allergens this table does not yet cover. Roughly 56 new Annex III entries are needed before the cosmetic scanner is complete.

Concentration is not on the label. EU rules require descending order only above 1%; below that the order is arbitrary. For every entry with dose_dependent true, the ingredient list cannot tell you whether the product is compliant, safe, or neither.

Hazard is not risk. Sodium hydroxide is caustic in a drum and inert at pH 5.5 in a finished lotion. Grading by intrinsic hazard rather than realistic exposure is the main reason ingredient-scoring apps get criticised by toxicologists.

EWG Skin Deep is not a peer of CIR, SCCS or FDA. It is a hazard-based advocacy score, not an exposure-based risk assessment, and it is the source of most of the disputed entries here. Decide deliberately whether Purla treats it as a source or as a competing viewpoint.

Some EU restrictions are environmental, not dermal — D5, D6, the microplastic phase-out and the PFAS proposals all restrict ingredients that regulators consider safe on skin. Presenting these as personal health risks misstates the finding.
Geography changes answers. Zinc pyrithione and coal tar are banned in EU cosmetics and legal in US OTC products. A single global grade will be wrong in one market.

authoritative_sources.CosIng: https://ec.europa.eu/growth/tools-databases/cosing/ — Annexes II-VI downloadable as CSV/XLS under Reference data. This is the machine-readable source of truth for the eu field.
authoritative_sources.SCCS: Scientific Committee on Consumer Safety opinions — the reasoning behind each Annex III/V/VI limit.
authoritative_sources.CIR: Cosmetic Ingredient Review (US industry-funded, peer-reviewed) — published safety assessments.
authoritative_sources.IFRA: Fragrance industry usage standards, stricter than EU law in places.

changelog: 0.4: added the EU 2023/1545 fragrance allergen set (Annex III entries 327-371) as corrected by Corrigendum OJ 2025/90876 of 11 Nov 2025. 40 entries added, 6 existing entries updated with annex refs, grouped declaration names and thresholds. 'Citrus Bergamia Peel Oil' renamed to the glossary name 'Citrus Aurantium Bergamia Peel Oil'. 'Citrus Aurantium Dulcis Peel Oil' demoted to a member_of pointer into entry 351 so it is no longer a competing independent record.

0.3: CosIng diff round 1. Sodium Hydroxymethylglycinate corrected to Annex II+V (conditional ban over a live authorisation). Seven Annex III entries added, three of them from the EU 2023/1545 fragrance allergen expansion. Two entries flagged for manual confirmation. normalise() no longer strips positional prefixes.
